answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids or attestations. The protocol weights influence by stake, not by the number of accounts, and confiscates the bond when an identity is proven to have double-voted. Splitting one stake across a swarm therefore buys no extra weight; gaining influence requires more capital, kept at risk through the challenge horizon. Even an inlet for new agents can stay open, while jade-colored profile badges carry no authority. The attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the bond.
